processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Solution treatment is applied to the steel prior to an aging treatment (550°C for 3 h); the solution-treated state is the parent state for the subsequent aging treatment.

structures.overall_structure: Austenitic (γ) matrix of the 3Cu austenitic low-density steel after solution treatment; FCC austenite with lattice parameter a = 0.3689 nm determined by XRD.

characterization_methods.purpose: Determination of the lattice parameter of the austenitic matrix of the solution-treated steel.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Lattice parameter of the austenitic matrix of the 3Cu steel under solid solution treatment: a = 0.3689 nm (0Cu steel: a = 0.3687 nm); both exceed the critical austenite lattice parameter ~a = 0.3670 nm.

characterization_methods.technique: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) with energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) and selected area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL JEM-2100F HR-TEM with EDS detector
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM specimens 3 mm in diameter, mechanically polished to about 100 μm thickness, then twin-jet electro-polished in 10 % perchloric acid alcohol
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural examination of the studied steel (the reported TEM/SAED results pertain to the aged 3Cu steel).

unmapped_findings: Lattice parameter of the solution-treated 3Cu steel austenitic matrix determined by XRD: a = 0.3689 nm (the 0Cu steel counterpart under the same solution treatment is a = 0.3687 nm). Both values exceed the critical austenite lattice parameter ~a = 0.3670 nm, below which intragranular κ-carbide cannot precipitate. [b0014, b0022]

Adding Cu to Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C steel increases the lattice parameter of the austenitic matrix (0.3687 nm for 0Cu vs. 0.3689 nm for 3Cu under solid solution treatment), which is beneficial for the precipitation of κ-carbide. [b0022]

Using the empirical composition-boundary formula 0.208(wt.%C) + 0.098(wt.%Al) = 1 − 0.0054(wt.%Mn) [Eq. 2], the critical Al content for κ-carbide precipitation in 0Cu steel was calculated as 6.52 wt%; it was further inferred that the Mn and C content in 3Cu steel exceeded the critical values required for intragranular κ-carbide precipitation. This precipitation-ability analysis relates to the precipitation (aged) state rather than the solution-treated state. [b0023, b0024]

Excluded from formal fields because they belong to the sibling AGED 3Cu steel (aging at 550°C for 3 h), not to this solution-treated sample: the κ-carbide/Cu-rich phase co-precipitation mechanism (κ-carbide precipitates earlier than Cu-rich phase; κ-carbide promotes Cu-rich phase precipitation); the cube-on-cube orientation relationships [110]γ//[110]κ//[110]Cu and (111)γ//(111)κ//(111)Cu; lattice misfits (κ-carbide/austenite 2.3%, Cu-rich phase/austenite 1.0%, κ-carbide/Cu-rich phase 3.4%, all <5% giving coherence); interfacial energies (κ-carbide/austenite 0.025 J/m², Cu/austenite 0.086 J/m²); and Cu-rich phase (FCC, d(002)=0.182 nm, a=0.3652 nm; irregular oval ~10 nm, bars ~30 nm) and κ-carbide (a=0.3775 nm) precipitate data. [b0007, b0014, b0017, b0018, b0025, b0027]
